data.reason: I stay with v1 (block_k 3) and follow the LLM's recommendation. Option 1 is clearly better for customers and for the KPI read under K1. On-time goes from 216.6 to 223.8 (+7.2, 5/5 seeds), late from 11.4 to 4.2, p95_wait_s from 138 to 110 and max_wait_s from 411 to 201, with unfinished at 0.0. It still lost the company vote (A ○, B ×, C ×). In D1 I declined to override a 1-2 vote on this same change and set two conditions: a remedy for C, and a breakdown of the added road violations. Neither has been met. C's utility would fall from 65.8 to 56.3, a drop of 9.5, and road violations would rise from 19.0 to 28.0 with no breakdown by company, type or severity. The Major eviction sanctions are believed to fall mostly on C, but that has not been checked. The larger rush-period gain does not change the governance judgment. It is the same change, the analysis is still missing, and it would be the first override of a two-of-three majority. Overriding now would also make the D1 conditions meaningless. The customer cost of waiting one more period is real: about 7.2 more late deliveries per run and a 411 s worst-case wait. I accept that cost so the change can return with a remedy and a breakdown, which could pass the vote or justify an informed override. Proposal 2 (hold_limit 60s → 50s, +0.4, 2/5 seeds) is not among the options here. D1.f1 and D1.f2 are not fulfilled by this decision and remain open. I add follow-ups for period 3.
assumptions: Rush-period demand is temporary or repeats, so the gain forgone this period can be recovered by a better-designed proposal later.
Keeping v1 does not worsen customer service beyond the measured current row.
B and C's votes reflect real costs, at least in part the eviction sanctions, rather than purely strategic opposition.
A variant of block_k=2 paired with a remedy for C is feasible and could win at least one of B or C.
unknowns: Per-company, per-type and per-severity breakdown of the road violations (19.0 → 28.0) and of the Major eviction sanctions under block_k=2.
Whether any remedy for C keeps most of the +7.2 on-time gain.
Why B votes against with only a -3.0 utility loss.
How long the rush demand lasts and what next period's demand looks like.
The safety significance of the additional road violations.
How customers perceive the 411 s worst-case wait.
